rules.description: Governance implementations must not import compiler or binding implementation modules.
Repository quality tooling must orchestrate contracts and processes rather than import a semantic compiler implementation.
A generated artifact must not appear among its own authoritative sources or generator inputs.
Implementation-derived test generation may remain compatibility evidence but cannot become normative or certification authority.
Contained-task records and templates must remain in designated governance locations.
New top-level implementation directories require an explicit architecture declaration.
Independent parser, compiler, and emitter implementations remain present across language bindings.
rules.rationale: The canonical compiler core and adapter migration have not begun, so prohibiting all binding semantic implementations would falsely certify the current architecture.
rules.retirement_condition: Activate binding-to-canonical-core dependency rules after each binding is migrated and its legacy semantic implementation is removed under contained verification.

rules.description: Shared expected semantic and diagnostic fixtures remain derived from TypeScript implementation behavior.
rules.rationale: The fixtures are necessary compatibility evidence but do not satisfy contract-first semantic authority.
rules.retirement_condition: Replace implementation-derived expected behavior with independently accepted specification-authored conformance contracts and deterministic projections.

rules.description: The editor tooling currently reaches STRling semantics through the Python binding and must migrate to the future canonical compiler interface.
rules.rationale: The LSP and its tests directly import Python-binding intelligence while no canonical compiler service exists; treating this as a current violation would begin the prohibited product migration.
rules.retirement_condition: After the canonical compiler interface exists, route editor semantics through that interface, remove direct STRling binding imports from tooling, and promote the rule to enforced.

rules.description: Specification schemas may reference only specification-owned schema contracts, never generated implementation output.
New parser, compiler, analyzer, planner, or emitter implementations under tooling require explicit architecture review.
Host-language bindings depend only on the stable canonical compiler interface for STRling semantics.
rules.rationale: No canonical compiler core exists yet and final-state enforcement would reject every current binding.
rules.activation_condition: Activate per binding only after canonical-core implementation, adapter migration, and behavior-preservation certification.
